title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection thresholds and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Summary: Improve the performance canary pipeline's automated regression detection and rollout guard logic to reduce false positives and enable safer canary rollouts. This change adjusts statistical thresholds, adds a hysteresis window, improves sample bucketing by model+seq_len, and introduces automatic rollback and staged escalation policies. Motivation: Over the last quarter we've had several noisy canary alerts and a couple of user-visible regressions where canary detection either flagged too aggressively on short bursts or failed to detect steady degradation in throughput. The goal is to make the detector both more sensitive to sustained regressions and less noisy for transient spikes. Design & changes: 1) Detection algorithm: switch to a two-tier EWMA + percentile baseline approach. We compute a rolling baseline percentile (p50/p95) per model+sequence-length bucket and track an EWMA-smoothed observed metric. Regression triggers when EWMA exceeds baseline by a configurable relative threshold and the effect size passes a minimum absolute delta. 2) Bucketing: group requests by model name and coarse sequence-length buckets (0-128,129-512,>512) to avoid mixing short/long tail latencies. 3) Minimum sample & confidence: require a minimum sample count (default 1000 requests) and at least 10 minutes of data before a canary alert; apply a bootstrap resampling step to estimate confidence intervals for small sample sizes. 4) Hysteresis & staging: add a hysteresis window (10 minutes) requiring sustained regression before triggering an automated rollback. Support staged escalation: WARN -> ALERT -> ROLLBACK based on duration and severity. 5) Rollout guards: integrate with rollout engine to pause/rollback canary, and to automatically reduce canary traffic to a safe fallback model variant when confidence is low. 6) Telemetry & dashboards: add new metrics (canary_detection_score, canary_sample_count, canary_hysteresis_remaining) and dashboard panels; add audit log entries for automated rollback decisions. 7) Config: expose thresholds and window sizes via canary policy proto with sensible defaults and runtime overrides. Testing & validation: - Unit tests for EWMA and bootstrap CI logic. - Synthetic traffic simulation harness updated to validate detection sensitivity and false-positive rate across 30k simulated windows. - Perf lab runs on representative models (gpt-like 7B, 13B) with real traffic traces; no regression in detection latency observed. - End-to-end staging rollout performed and monitored for 48h. Rollout plan: feature flagged by default; gradual rollout to production canaries for 10% of canary runs for 72h, then increase to 50% if metrics are stable. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests updated - [x] Perf lab validation - [x] Docs updated in observability-pack - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Added dashboards & alerts Notes: This PR focuses on canary detection and guard behavior only; it does not change core serving runtime kernels. Related tickets: ENG-5274 (canary false positives), ENG-5330 (canary hysteresis), PM-214 (canary UX improvements).
